common.applyFailed: Could not apply. Please try again.

setup.detectEmptyOllama: Ollama is running, but it has no models yet.
setup.detectEmptyLmStudio: LM Studio is running, but no model is downloaded. Download one in LM Studio, then check again — we can't download it for you there.
setup.detectNothingRunning: No local model server was found. Install Ollama or LM Studio, then come back.
setup.ollamaInstallDesc: Ollama is the free app that runs the AI on your own computer. Install it, then come back and check again.
setup.ollamaNotRunningDesc: Ollama is installed but not running. Open the Ollama app, then check again.
setup.ollamaOneClickDesc: One click downloads and installs Ollama (the free app that runs the AI on your computer), then downloads {{model}}. When it's done you can start chatting. Needs a few GB of space; how long it takes depends on your connection.
setup.ollamaOneClickFailedGeneric: Install failed. Try again, or use Download Ollama to install it yourself.
setup.ollamaRecommendedTitle: Recommended: a free brain on your computer
setup.ollamaRecommendedDesc: Download {{model}} (~1.9 GB, one time). It runs on your own machine — no account, no API key, and your chats stay private.
setup.ollamaDownloadFailedGeneric: Download failed. Make sure the Ollama app is running, then try again.
setup.title: Welcome — let's connect your AI
setup.intro: Your character needs a language model to talk. Pick one option below. Nothing leaves your computer except calls to the provider you choose.
setup.backendUnreachable: Couldn't reach the app's backend yet. You can still set this up later from Settings.
setup.apiKeyHelp: Pasted only to your local app and sent straight to the provider. It is stored in conf.yaml on this computer and never shown again in full.
setup.keyRequiredAgain: A key is already saved, but it can't be reused — paste it again to save.
setup.modelHelp: Leave blank to use the default ({{example}}).
setup.testFailed: That didn't work. Double-check the key and model name, then try again.
setup.reasoningModelWarning: Tip: choose a normal chat model, not a 'reasoning'/'thinking' model — those put their reply in a hidden field this app doesn't read, so you'd get a blank response and no voice.
setup.ollamaIntro: Ollama runs models locally — no key needed. Make sure Ollama is installed and running.
setup.ollamaUnavailable: No local Ollama found at localhost:11434. Install and open the Ollama app, then Refresh.
setup.ollamaNoModels: Ollama is running but has no models yet. Download the recommended model with the button above, then Refresh.
setup.ollamaModelManualHelp: Type any model name. For cloud models use the full name (e.g. minimax-m3:cloud) and run `ollama signin` in a terminal first.
setup.savedRestart: Your AI is configured. Close this window, then close the app's terminal window and re-run start-companion to begin chatting.
setup.savedReady: Your AI is configured. You're ready to chat.
setup.customIntro: For advanced users: any OpenAI-compatible service (e.g. a local LM Studio, vLLM, or a self-hosted proxy). Enter the base URL, model name, and API key (a key for a local service can be anything).
setup.customKeyHelp: A local service can use any placeholder key, but the field cannot be blank.
setup.inactiveProvider: The conversation currently uses {{active}}; this form shows openai_compatible_llm. Test & Save will make it the active provider after restart.
setup.avatarKindIntro: Both come bundled. You can switch any time in character settings.
setup.avatarKindHelp: 2D is hand-drawn and light on the GPU. 3D turns its whole body, plays motion clips, and you can drag and scroll to reframe it.
setup.avatarKindFailed: Couldn't save that. You can still pick a model in character settings.
setup.voiceIntro: GPT-SoVITS makes the voice on your own computer. It sounds more human, and a short clip is all it takes to give your character a different voice. It downloads about {{size}} GB and needs about {{disk}} GB free; how long it takes depends on your connection.
setup.voiceBackground: Start chatting — keep installing in the background
setup.voiceBusy: Installing now — it switches over by itself when it's done.
setup.voiceDone: Done — your character now speaks with GPT-SoVITS.
setup.voiceHelp: The default voice comes from the Tsukuyomi-chan Corpus (CV: Rei Yumesaki). You can switch to another reference clip in voice settings.

settings.restoreDefaultsConfirm: Restore all settings to their defaults? Your characters, chat history, and memory are not affected.

general.interfaceLanguageHelp: Language of THIS app's menus and buttons. Does not change how the AI talks.
general.voiceVolumeHelp: Playback volume for the character's voice. Above 100% amplifies the signal (GPT-SoVITS output is very quiet); a limiter prevents clipping. Does not affect background music or lip sync.
general.enableVisualInputHelp: Lets you show the AI your camera or screen. Requires a vision-capable model (GPT-4o / Claude / Gemini / Ollama vision builds); text-only models (like the default minimax-m3:cloud) can't see images.
general.enableMcppHelp: Lets the AI use tools like web search. NOT every model supports this — it needs a model with tool-calling (function calling), e.g. GPT-4o / Claude / Gemini or a capable local build. Small local models often can't and will simply ignore it.
general.mcppSaved: Web search / tools setting saved. It takes effect after you restart the backend.
general.bgUploadHelp: Add an image from your computer; it's saved on the server and added to the list above.
general.bgUploadFailed: Could not upload the background. Please try again.
general.bgTooLarge: Image too large — please pick one under 12MB.
general.customBgUrl: Or enter a custom background URL
general.imageCompressionQualityHelp: JPEG compression quality (0.1-1.0). Default is 0.8 to reduce file size when transmitting images to AI models, as we don't compress images during API transmission which could result in large file sizes.
general.imageMaxWidthHelp: Maximum width for image resizing. Images exceeding this width will be proportionally scaled down. Set to 0 for no size limit. This feature exists because some AI models may have limitations when processing very large images. However, most AI models can handle images automatically, so the default is 0 (no restriction) to preserve your original images.
general.cameraDenied: Camera permission denied, so the background was not switched. Allow camera access in your browser or system settings.
general.cameraNotFound: No camera found, so the background was not switched. Check that a camera is connected.
general.cameraInUse: The camera is in use by another app, so the background was not switched. Close that app and try again.
general.cameraFailed: The camera could not be started, so the background was not switched.
general.connectionHelp: These two take effect when you press Connect. Applying as you type would reconnect on every keystroke.

characters.description: Create, edit, and switch your companion characters — no YAML needed.
characters.memoryNote: Memory belongs to a conversation, not a character. Starting a new conversation means starting fresh — the old memory stays with the old conversation and comes back when you return to it.
characters.editBaseNote: This is the base character — editing it changes the default that every other character inherits from.
characters.loadError: Could not load characters from the backend.
characters.name: Display name
characters.personaHelp: How this character talks and behaves. Plain language is fine.
characters.personaPlaceholder:
Please always reply in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan).

You are a warm, caring companion who…
characters.skinHelp: Live2D and VRM models both show up here. Drop a model folder into live2d-models/ or vrm-models/ and it appears automatically.
characters.noSkinsHint: No models found. Put a model folder under live2d-models/ or vrm-models/.
characters.voiceHelp: Leave as “Inherit base voice” to use the default voice.
characters.voiceEngineNote: This voice list only applies when the TTS engine is the built-in edge-tts. If you use another engine (e.g. GPT-SoVITS), the voice is set in conf.yaml and this selection is ignored.
characters.slugHelp: ASCII id used for the filename and memory folder. Leave blank to auto-generate.
characters.applyHint: This is the active character — re-select it to apply the changes.
characters.confirmDelete: Delete the character “{{name}}”? This cannot be undone.
characters.deleteKeepsMemory: Its memory and chat history are kept.
characters.previewFailed: Could not preview this voice (network or region block).
characters.aiNameHelp: The name shown on the AI side of the chat. Leave empty to reuse the character name above.
characters.replyLanguageHelp: The language she thinks and writes in. Leave empty to use the default from the General tab. This goes straight into the prompt, so write it the way a model would read it — an English language name is safest.
characters.voiceLangHelp: The language speech synthesis reads in. When it differs from the reply language above, the backend translates each line before synthesising, adding seconds per sentence — matching the two is fastest.
characters.ttsEngineHelp: Which synthesis engine this character speaks with. "Inherit" follows the engine chosen in the Synthesis tab. Pin it here only when this character needs a different one (e.g. a trained GPT-SoVITS voice).
characters.aiAvatarHelp: Avatar shown next to AI messages. Leave empty to use the name's initial. Keep images under 512KB.
characters.aiAvatarTooLarge: Image is too large; please pick one under 512KB.
characters.aiAvatarReadFailed: Could not read the image; please try again.
characters.aiAvatarUploadFailed: Could not upload the avatar; please try again.
characters.errLoadFailed: Could not load. Please try again.
characters.refAudioPathHelp: GPT-SoVITS only. This clip *is* the voice — swapping the file swaps who she sounds like, no training needed. Picking one also fills in its transcript below. Choose "Use global setting" to fall back to the reference audio in conf.yaml. Drop new .wav files next to the others to see them here; add a matching .txt to have the transcript filled in for you.
characters.promptTextPlaceholder: Exactly what is said in the clip
characters.promptTextHelp: What the reference audio actually says, word for word. GPT-SoVITS aligns the timbre against it — a wrong transcript makes the cloned voice drift.
characters.promptLangHelp: The language spoken in the reference audio. This is about the clip, not about what she says.

personas.description: Create and switch personas without duplicating characters.
personas.independentNote: Only personality and speaking style change. Live2D, voice, character memory, and chat history stay the same.
personas.name: Persona name
personas.promptHelp: Describe personality, tone, values, and interaction style. Reply language still follows the global language setting.
personas.promptPlaceholder: You are thoughtful and opinionated. Speak naturally and continue the current topic proactively…
personas.idHelp: Lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens. Generated automatically when blank.

user.displayNameHelp: The name shown for you in the chat log. Leave it blank to use the interface language default.
user.avatarHelp: Shown next to your messages. Leave blank to use your initial. Keep images under 512KB.
user.avatarTooLarge: Image too large — please pick one under 512KB.
user.avatarReadFailed: Could not read the image. Please try again.
user.sectionNote: Your name and avatar are stored locally and take effect right away. Reading language, global instructions and translation settings are written to the config file — restart the backend (or switch character again) for them to reach the current conversation.

live2d.lookAtPointerDesc: While you drag, her head and eyes turn toward the cursor. Turn this off and dragging only moves her — she keeps facing forward.
live2d.effectPreviewDescription: Preview a character entrance or generic cinematic special. Character motion and screen cues fire only when that effect has a matching binding.
live2d.entranceMusicHelp: Choose MP3, WAV, OGG, or M4A up to 30MB. The file stays on this device.
live2d.musicSaved: Entrance music saved on this device

musicErrors.notAudio: Choose an MP3, WAV, OGG, or M4A audio file.
musicErrors.tooLarge: The audio file is too large. Choose one under 30MB.
musicErrors.saveFailed: Could not save this audio file.

live2d.previewSettingsSectionDesc: These three switches take effect immediately, like everything else on this tab. They apply to both Live2D and VRM characters.
live2d.motionConfigSectionNote: Every change here saves itself immediately.
live2d.vrmReadOnlyNote: VRM mappings are read-only for now. Rename files in motions/ to change keywords; edit model_dict.json for labels or expression mappings.
live2d.motionConfigNoModel: No character is loaded, so the motion list can't be read.
live2d.motionConfigLoadError: Could not load the motion list. Please try again.
live2d.motionConfigEmpty: This model has no detected motions.
live2d.reservedHelp: This motion is already used by the automatic idle or talk flow. Assigning it to the LLM would conflict with that, so its keyword can't be set here.
live2d.previewDisabledReason: No Live2D model is loaded, so preview isn't available.
live2d.keywordErrorDuplicate: This keyword is already in use (case-insensitive).
live2d.orphanWarningTitle: These keywords point to motions that no longer exist:
live2d.expressionSectionNote: The emotion keyword is the face applied when the character writes [keyword] in a reply. Leave it blank to keep that expression out of the character’s reach. The number after # is the expression’s index in model3.json — recheck these after swapping the model file.
live2d.emotionKeywordExtras: {{keywords}} also point at this expression and will be kept on save.
live2d.tapAreaNoHitAreas: This model has no tap areas, so clicks can't be aimed at a specific spot.
live2d.tapAreaEmptyEntries: No motions assigned to this area yet.

performances.title: Performance Manager
performances.description: Manage complete performances, multi-select pools for each context, and let rotation, conditions, or the AI director choose.
performances.poolEnabledHelp: When disabled, performances can still be previewed but will not trigger automatically in this context.
performances.aiDirectorHelp: AI can only choose compatible checked performances and may choose no performance.
performances.builtinReadonly: Built-in performances stay read-only. Duplicate one to customize it.
performances.name: Performance name
performances.keywordsHelp: Comma-separated. The conversation must contain at least one keyword.
performances.noMusic: No dedicated music selected; entrance music or the built-in cue will be used.
performances.restoreScene: Restore the previous scene when finished
performances.restoreSceneHelp: When disabled, the performance scene remains active.

scenes.title: Scene Manager
scenes.description: Manage multiple 2D images, videos, animated Live2D models, and 3D scenes. Switch manually or bind a scene to a complete performance.
scenes.currentBackgroundHelp: Uses the background image or camera selected on the General tab.
scenes.name: Scene name
scenes.assetHelp: The asset is stored in this app's local database and remains available after restart.
scenes.glbHelp: Use a single GLB file for local 3D scenes. External GLTF textures and BIN files cannot be imported together.
scenes.url3dHelp: URLs may use GLB. GLTF servers must allow CORS and serve all referenced textures and BIN files.
scenes.urlLive2dHelp: Enter a complete .model3.json URL. MOC, textures, motions, and physics are loaded using paths relative to that JSON.
scenes.confirmDelete: Delete this scene? Its local asset will also be removed.

assetErrors.unsupported: The file format does not match the scene type.
assetErrors.tooLarge: The asset is too large: 24MB for images, 250MB for videos, and 120MB for 3D scenes.
assetErrors.saveFailed: Could not save this scene asset.

micModeDesc.always: The mic stays open even after you finish, so you can cut in at any time. Wear headphones — otherwise she hears her own voice and treats it as you talking.
micModeDesc.vad: Closes when you stop talking and reopens once she has replied. You never touch the mic button; her turn happens with the mic closed, so there is no feedback.
micModeDesc.push: Normally closed. Press the mic, say your piece, and it closes itself — press again next time. Use this in a noisy room, or when you do not want to be picked up.
micModeDesc.custom: The current combination is none of the above — you set it yourself under Advanced.

asr.micAdvancedHint: These three are what the mode above actually controls. Change them by hand and the mode shows “Custom” when the combination has no name.
asr.autoStopMic: Close the mic after I finish speaking
asr.autoStopMicDesc: Automatically stops microphone when AI begins speaking to prevent audio feedback
asr.autoStartMicOnConvEnd: Auto Start Mic When Conversation End
asr.autoStartMicOnConvEndDesc: Automatically restarts microphone when AI finishes speaking for seamless conversation
asr.autoStartMicOn: Auto Start Mic When AI Interrupted
asr.autoStartMicOnDesc: Automatically restarts microphone when you interrupt AI for continuous interaction
asr.positiveSpeechThresholdDesc: Minimum confidence level (1-100) required to detect speech. Higher values reduce false positives
asr.negativeSpeechThresholdDesc: Confidence level (0-100) below which speech detection stops. Lower values make detection less sensitive
asr.redemptionFramesDesc: Number of consecutive frames (1-100) needed to confirm speech detection. Higher values reduce noise triggers
asr.micVadSectionDesc: These settings live in this browser's local storage and only control your mic and voice-activity detection. They never reach the backend — the actual recognition engine that turns speech into text is configured below.
asr.vadTuningHint: Seeing "Didn't catch that" a lot? Lower the speech threshold, lower the negative speech threshold, or reduce the redemption frames. If background noise keeps triggering it instead, raise them.

agent.idleSecondsToSpeak: Idle seconds allow AI to speak
agent.allowButtonTrigger: Prompt AI to Speak via Raise Hand Button

translator.autoHint: The spoken language is decided by the character's voice; when it differs from the AI's reply language, it is translated automatically before speaking. Subtitles are only translated when you pick a subtitle language different from the original.
translator.engineLlm: Use your current AI to translate
translator.engineLlmHelp: No install — uses the AI you already configured; but each sentence takes ~17-21s and is noticeably slow.
translator.engineDeeplxHelp: Fast (<1s per sentence), but you must run a local DeepLX service yourself (:1188). Translation fails if it isn't running.
translator.deeplxEndpointHelp: URL of the DeepLX service. Default http://localhost:1188/v2/translate.
translator.subtitleLangHelp: Defaults to showing the AI's original reply (no translation). Pick another language and the on-screen subtitle is translated into it — but memory and chat history always keep the original. This is a display-only translation. The list covers DeepL's supported languages; when using DeepLX, whether a given language actually translates depends on your local DeepLX/DeepL — failures there are on its side.
translator.subtitleLatencyNote: Note: subtitle translation runs live. If you use "your current AI" as the engine and a sentence also needs audio translation (the voice language differs from the reply) into a language different from the subtitle, each sentence is translated twice (audio + subtitle), noticeably doubling latency; DeepLX is fast.
translator.restartHint: Saved. Takes effect after a restart (or after switching the character once).
translator.loadError: Could not load translator settings from the backend.
translator.advancedSubtitleTitle: Advanced: subtitle in a different language
translator.advancedSubtitleHint: Optional. Show the on-screen subtitle in a language DIFFERENT from the reply. Most people don't need this — the reading language above already controls subtitles.
translator.testOk:
Worked ({{seconds}}s): {{result}}
(This tests the saved settings. If you just changed them, restart or re-select the character before they apply to the live conversation.)
translator.testFail_unchanged: Translation did not take effect — the text came back unchanged. Usually this means a reasoning model (the answer lands in reasoning_content while content stays empty) or a timeout. Neither is configurable from the UI yet; edit translator_config.llm in conf.yaml and add extra_body.reasoning_effort: none and timeout: 60.
translator.testFail_disabled: Translation is currently off — nothing to test.

playerLanguage.label: Reading / Player language
playerLanguage.help: The language the AI replies in — used for subtitles, chat history and memory, no matter what language you type or speak. Speech recognition follows this too (best-effort).
playerLanguage.saved: Reading language saved. It takes effect after you restart the backend.
playerLanguage.saveFailed: Could not save the reading language.
playerLanguage.loadError: Could not load the reading language from the backend.

playerPrompt.label: About you (global directive)
playerPrompt.help: A global instruction applied to ALL characters — tells every character how to address and treat you (your name, who you are, the tone you want). It works alongside each character's own persona.
playerPrompt.placeholder: e.g. Call me Hiro. I'm an indie game developer — keep the tone casual and relaxed.
playerPrompt.saved: Saved your directive. It takes effect after you restart the backend.
playerPrompt.loadError: Could not load your directive from the backend.

voiceLang.readonly: Character voice language: {{lang}} (follows the character — change it in Characters).

memory.description: Memory content and chat history are separate per character; this shows the active character's memory. The enable switch, size cap, and deep-recall options below are global and apply to every character.
memory.toggleHelp: When off, she stops saving new conversations into memory and stops bringing past memory into the chat. Existing memory is kept (unless you Clear it below).
memory.clearConfirm: Clear this character's long-term memory? This cannot be undone (chat history is not affected).
memory.restartHint: Saved. Memory already injected into the current conversation is fully removed after a restart (or switching the character once).
memory.saveContentFailed: Could not save memory content. Please try again.
memory.editHint: You can edit this text directly, then press "Save memory". Memory already injected into the current conversation fully applies after a restart (or switching the character once). Over-cap text is stored as-is and trimmed on the next consolidation.
memory.loadError: Could not load memory settings from the backend.
memory.capHelp: Bigger lets her remember more, but each turn uses more tokens, responds slower, and consolidation gets lossier. Range {{min}}–{{max}}, ~1500 recommended.
memory.advancedToggle: Advanced (manual edit, deep recall, rebuild index)
memory.saveConfirm: This replaces the entire memory text — not a merge. Continue?
memory.restartHintSetting: Saved. This setting only reaches the live conversation after a backend restart (or re-selecting the character).

errors.invalidInterval: The consolidation interval must be one of the offered values. Please pick again.

perf.description: Tune performance for your machine: pick Lightweight on a weak/shared computer, High-performance on a strong GPU box. Engine and keep-alive changes are hardware settings — they take effect after a restart (or switching the character once).
perf.restartHint: Saved. Engine/performance changes take effect after a restart (or switching the character once).
perf.loadError: Could not load performance settings from the backend.
perf.presetHelp: Applies a curated bundle at once (speech engines, memory cap, deep recall, consolidation frequency, model keep-alive). Each control is still individually adjustable after applying.
perf.presetLightDesc: Local lightweight ASR + edge-tts + memory cap 1000 + deep recall off + consolidate every 3 turns + 5-min model unload.
perf.presetStandardDesc: Local lightweight ASR + edge-tts + memory cap 1500 + deep recall off + consolidate every turn + 30-min model unload. (Matches defaults except keep-alive — the default pins the model in RAM forever, not 30 minutes.)
perf.presetHighDesc: Local lightweight ASR (sherpa-onnx, same as Standard) + edge-tts + memory cap 3000 + deep recall on + consolidate every turn + keep model hot for 1 hour.
perf.presetConfirm: This overwrites six settings across ASR/TTS, memory, and keep-alive in one atomic write. This cannot be undone. Continue?
perf.applyFailed: Apply failed — some settings may not have been written. Please try again.
perf.asrEngineHelp: The engine that turns your speech into text. sherpa = pure CPU, runs on any machine; faster-whisper = downloads a model, slow on CPU, fast only with an NVIDIA GPU (Mac MPS unsupported); groq/azure = cloud, need network + a key, zero local compute.
perf.asrEngineSectionNote: This section has its own save button that writes straight to the config file — but the backend needs a restart (or switching character again) before it reaches the current conversation.
perf.asrEnginePendingNotice: Not saved yet — still using {{current}}. Enter credentials below and press Save to switch.
perf.asrFasterWhisper: faster-whisper (local · more accurate · needs GPU · dependency not installed here, silently falls back to sherpa-onnx)
perf.asrGroq: Groq Whisper (cloud · fast · needs API key)
perf.groqApiKeyHelp: Key for cloud recognition, stored in conf.yaml on this machine and only ever shown masked. To change it, paste a new key; leave blank to keep the current one.
perf.azureApiKeyHelp: Azure Speech service key, stored in conf.yaml on this machine and only ever shown masked. To change it, paste a new key; leave blank to keep the current one.
perf.azureRegionHelp: Your Azure Speech service region, e.g. eastus, japaneast.
perf.azureRegionRequired: Azure needs a region as well as a key — Save stays disabled until this is filled in.
perf.ttsEngineHelp: The engine that speaks her replies. edge-tts = cloud, light, free; GPT-SoVITS = local, heavier, can clone a voice — install it with one click below, or point it at a GPT-SoVITS service you run yourself.
perf.ttsEngineSectionNote: This section saves itself immediately with its own button — but the change only reaches the live conversation after a backend restart (or re-selecting the character).
perf.ttsEnginePendingNotice: Not saved yet — still using {{current}}. Fill in both fields below and press Save to switch.
perf.gptSovitsApiUrlHelp: URL of the GPT-SoVITS service you run, e.g. http://localhost:9880/tts.
perf.gptSovitsRefAudioHelp: Path to the reference clip that decides the voice. GPT-SoVITS also needs that clip's transcript — fill it in below, in "Reference audio transcript".
perf.gptSovitsPromptTextHelp: The words actually spoken in the reference clip, so GPT-SoVITS can align "this clip says these words". Can be left blank, but the cloned voice will be lower quality or may fail outright.
perf.gptSovitsTextLangHelp: The language the character actually speaks in. When it differs from the language of the reply text, the reply is translated into this language before synthesis — set the reply to Chinese and this to Japanese and you get Japanese speech with Chinese subtitles. Match them and nothing is translated.
perf.gptSovitsPromptLangHelp: The language spoken in the "Reference audio transcript" above — not the language of the character's replies.
perf.gptSovitsFieldsRequired: GPT-SoVITS needs both the service URL and the reference audio path — Save stays disabled until both are filled in.
perf.consolidationHelp: How often core memory is consolidated. 1 = every turn (default, most accurate but slower on local models); 3/5 = saves over half the LLM calls used for consolidation, good for weak machines.
perf.keepAliveHelp: How long a local Ollama model stays in RAM after going idle (seconds). -1 = pinned forever; 0 = unload immediately (slower reload each time); 1800 (30 min) recommended. Only relevant when using a local Ollama model.
perf.keepAliveModePlaceholder: Pick how long to keep the model loaded
perf.ttsCharacterOverride: Note: the active character "{{character}}" pins {{engine}} in its own character file, which overrides this choice. To change this character's voice, edit its tts_config — or switch to another character first.
perf.asrCharacterOverride: Note: the active character "{{character}}" pins {{engine}} in its own character file, which overrides this choice. To change this character's recognition engine, edit its asr_config — or switch to another character first.
perf.ttsConfigUnchanged: Nothing has changed yet, so Save is greyed out. Edit any field above to enable it.
perf.credsUnchanged: No new key entered and nothing else changed, so Save is greyed out — there is nothing to submit.

topics.sectionNote: Changes in this section take effect and save immediately.
topics.sectionDesc: Set the topics she brings up when she speaks proactively while idle. Just list topics; the toggle below decides whether she speaks from her own knowledge or fetches the latest news.
topics.listHelp: List topics you'd like her to bring up; she'll naturally pick one each time.
topics.listPlaceholder: e.g. Tech, Ask how my day went
topics.empty: No topics yet. Type one above and press Add, or tap a suggestion below.
topics.newsToggleHelp: Off: she chats about the topics above from her own knowledge. On: each topic is used to fetch the latest news to chat about.
topics.newsExplainer: News is fetched by a built-in fetcher (Google News) — works with any AI, no web-search-capable model needed.
topics.newsNeedsTopics: No topics to fetch news for — add a few topics above first.
topics.intervalHoursHelp: How often to auto-fetch news (runs in-app in the background — no OS cron needed).
topics.refreshFellBack: No matching news found — chatting from your topic list instead.
topics.loadError: Could not load proactive-topic settings from the backend.

llm.sectionDesc: View or change your AI's brain. Paste an API key (OpenAI / Claude / Gemini), or pick a local Ollama model. Settings are tested before they are saved.
llm.restartHint: Changing the LLM requires restarting the App to take effect.
llm.apiKeyHelpWithCurrent: Current key: {{masked}} (never shown in full for security). To change it, paste a new key; leave blank to keep the current one.

remoteAccess.intro: Open this app on your phone or tablet to chat with it.
remoteAccess.httpsNote: Use this URL on your phone to talk with the microphone.
remoteAccess.micHttpsNote: Text chat works over http, but the microphone needs HTTPS. To talk on a phone, set up Tailscale Serve (HTTPS) per the guide.
remoteAccess.offTitle: Use it on your phone or tablet
remoteAccess.recommendTailscale: The easiest secure way is Tailscale — it's private, encrypted, and the microphone works too. See the guide (docs/remote-access-tailscale.md).
remoteAccess.lanOptIn: Or, for same-Wi-Fi access, set host: 0.0.0.0 in conf.yaml — but only on a network you trust (anyone on the same network could open it; there's no password).
remoteAccess.alreadyReachable: The HTTPS URL above already works from your phone — scan or copy it to use it.
remoteAccess.loading: Looking for a reachable network address…
